The short clinical answer for your awareness as a trainer:

A C-section is abdominal surgery — the rectus abdominis, fascia, and deeper layers are cut and sutured. Standard return-to-core guidance from pelvic floor physiotherapists is:

- Weeks 1–6: diaphragmatic breathing and pelvic floor activation only. No loaded or flexion-based ab work. This is already in Phase 1 of the programme.
- Week 6 check: OB clears general activity. This does not automatically clear loaded core work.
- Pelvic floor physio assessment: strongly recommended before any direct ab programming. She should be screened for diastasis recti (abdominal separation), which is common post-C-section and contraindicated for crunches, sit-ups, and many plank progressions until resolved.
- Typically 8–12 weeks post-surgery minimum before dead_bug, bird_dog, and side_plank progressions are appropriate — which is why Phase 2 of this programme introduces them gradually from week 7 onward.
- Loaded flexion work (crunch, sit_up, v_up) should not be added to this programme without written pelvic floor physio clearance specific to this client.

Instruct your client to obtain a pelvic floor physiotherapy assessment at or after her six-week OB check before you progress her core work beyond what is already in this programme.
